newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks end bourse trade flat, rally wanes.
newsitem.headline: German stocks end bourse trade flat, rally wanes.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade flat on Tuesday after the rallies seen in the last two trading days began to wane and dealers said there was now the possibility of a small correction in stock values.
The DAX index of 30 blue chip German shares closed 1.79 points or 0.07 percent lower at 2,628.08 on volumes described by dealers as particularly thin.
"Some market players clearly do not trust recent developments too much, there is a degree of scepticism out there," one said, forecasting light morning losses.

But he added that the fact the rally -- based largely on sentiment that U.S. interest rates were now not likely to move upwards as fast as some had been predicting -- had taken some players by surprise meant that some follow-through buying could lend further support to the market.

U.S. August capacity utilisation and industrial production figures due at 1315 GMT, while not as critical for inflation as last week's consumer and producer price data, were seen as having a possible effect on the market later on.

Movements among individual stocks were limited. Deutsche Bank ended 25 pfennigs higher at 72.70 after comments made at an analyst meeting that recent problems with its London-based Morgan Grenfell unit would not affect earnings.
